problems.title: Use the difference of cubes
problems.question: If $s^3-t^3=18$ and $s^2+st+t^2=12$, find s-t.
problems.idea: Factor the first expression using the second.
steps: Since 12 is nonzero, divide both sides by 12.

problems.title: Two exterior angles determine the third interior angle
problems.question: Two exterior angles of a triangle sum to 200°. Find the remaining interior angle.
problems.idea: Convert the exterior angles into their adjacent interior angles.
formulas: An interior angle and its adjacent exterior angle sum to 180°; triangle angles sum to 180°.
steps: The corresponding two interior angles sum to 360°-200°=160°.

problems.title: Degree after cancellation
problems.question: Find the degree of $(2x-y)^2-(y+2x)^2+8xy+17$.
problems.idea: Simplify before reading the degree.
steps: The difference of squares of the two binomials is -8xy.
A nonzero constant polynomial has degree 0.

problems.title: Cancel the squared terms
problems.question: Simplify $2(2a-3b)(2a+3b)-(2a+b)^2-(2a-b)^2$.
problems.idea: Use a difference of squares and a sum of two squares.
steps: The two subtracted squares sum to 8a²+2b².

problems.title: Apply the difference of squares twice
problems.question: Simplify $(x-y)(x^2+y^2)(x+y)$.
problems.idea: Multiply the first and last factors first.

problems.title: Three exterior angles form a full turn
problems.question: One exterior angle of a triangle is twice a second and 30° smaller than a third. Find the smallest.
problems.idea: Express all three exterior angles in terms of the smallest.
formulas: One exterior angle at each vertex sums to 360°.
steps: Let the smallest exterior angle be x. The other two are 2x and 2x+30°.

problems.title: Recognize a squared difference
problems.question: Evaluate $(2a+5)^2-2(2a+5)(2a-7)+(2a-7)^2$.
problems.idea: Treat the two long binomials as single quantities.

problems.title: Two half-hypotenuse lengths
problems.question: In a right triangle with a 30° angle, how many times the median to the hypotenuse is the sum of the hypotenuse and the leg opposite 30°?
problems.idea: Both the shorter leg and that median equal half the hypotenuse.
formulas: A 30°-opposite leg=c/2; the right-angle median to the hypotenuse=c/2.
steps: Write the hypotenuse as c. The requested numerator is c+c/2=3c/2.

problems.title: A polynomial with disappearing quadratic terms
problems.question: Simplify $x(1-2x)-(x-3)(x+3)+3x^2$.
problems.idea: Expand each product and combine like terms.

problems.title: Bound the sum of two diagonals
problems.question: A convex quadrilateral has side lengths 1,2,3,4. Which listed value can the sum of its diagonals have: 2.3,3.8,4.6,5,6.9,11?
problems.idea: Compare its diagonals with the perimeter.
formulas: Triangle inequality: each side is less than the sum of the two segments joining its endpoints to the diagonals’ intersection.
steps: Let the diagonals meet at O. Applying the triangle inequality to the four small triangles gives perimeter<2(AC+BD).
Each diagonal is shorter than either of the two boundary paths joining its endpoints; in particular their sum is below the perimeter 10.
Only 6.9 lies strictly between 5 and 10 among the choices.
problems.note: The side lengths are given without a required cyclic order. They can be arranged to attain this value; the bounds eliminate all the other listed choices.

problems.title: Cancel the product terms
problems.question: Calculate $(a+1)(b+1)-(a-1)(b-1)$ if a+b=9.
problems.idea: Expand and group a and b.
steps: The first product is ab+a+b+1. The second is ab-a-b+1.

problems.title: Factor a sum of cubes with a common quadratic
problems.question: Factor $x^3+y^3+2x^2-2xy+2y^2$.
problems.idea: The first two terms and the last three terms share the same quadratic factor.

problems.title: Find a difference from a known product
problems.question: If $25x^2-y^2=40$ and 5x+y=10, find 15x-3y.
problems.idea: Factor the difference of squares.
problems.note: The highlighted 7 in the printed key does not satisfy this calculation.

problems.title: Complete a nearby square
problems.question: Which listed number replaces * in 625+100+* to make a perfect square?
problems.idea: Find the nearest square above 725.

problems.title: Reflection pairs of congruent triangles
problems.question: C and D lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB; K is its intersection with AB, with C between K and D. All the shown connecting segments are drawn. How many pairs of congruent triangles are forced by the figure?
problems.idea: Reflection in the perpendicular bisector swaps A and B and fixes C,D,K.
formulas: Reflection preserves all lengths and angles, so reflected triangles are congruent.
steps: Triangle AKC is paired with BKC.
Triangle AKD is paired with BKD.
Triangle ACD is paired with BCD.
ABC and ABD reflect onto themselves rather than a different triangle.

problems.title: Substitute into a perfect square
problems.question: Find $25a^2-40ab+16b^2$ when a=10,b=12.
problems.idea: Recognize the square before substituting.

problems.title: Data sufficient to construct a triangle
problems.question: Which listed data determine a triangle: three angles; two angles and one side; one angle and two sides; or three side lengths?
problems.idea: For the standard construction criterion, two valid angles and a side determine shape and size.
formulas: Two positive angles with sum below 180° determine the third; ASA or AAS fixes a unique triangle.
steps: Three angles determine only shape, with no fixed scale.
Two valid angles and one positive side give a unique construction.
Arbitrary three side lengths can violate the triangle inequality; an arbitrary side-side-angle specification can fail or be ambiguous.
problems.answer: Two angles and one side, assuming valid triangle angles.
problems.note: The word “always” still presupposes valid data: positive angles whose sum is below 180°, and a positive side length.

problems.title: Square a factored polynomial
problems.question: Which identity correctly expands $(x^2y+xy^2)^2$?
problems.idea: Factor out xy before squaring.

problems.title: A point on a perpendicular bisector
problems.question: In ABC, AB=BC=10 and AC=2. K is the midpoint of BC. The perpendicular to BC at K meets AB at M. Find the perimeter of AMC.
problems.idea: M is equally far from B and C.
formulas: Any point on a segment’s perpendicular bisector is equidistant from its endpoints.
steps: Because M lies on AB, AM+MB=AB=10.

problems.title: An altitude meets an angle bisector
problems.question: In ABC, A=40° and B=80°. Altitude AK and internal bisector BM meet at O. Find angle MOK.
problems.idea: Find the acute line angle first, then use the requested rays.
formulas: BM makes B/2=40° with BC; AK is perpendicular to BC.
steps: The acute angle between the lines BM and AK is 90°-40°=50°.
In the triangle’s configuration, OM points toward AC while OK points down to BC.
The requested angle is the supplementary one: 180°-50°=130°.

problems.title: A parallelogram inside an isosceles triangle
problems.question: ABC is isosceles with base AC and AB=6. From D on AC draw DE∥BC and DF∥AB, meeting AB and BC at E,F. Find the perimeter of EBFD.
problems.idea: Use the small isosceles triangle and the interior parallelogram.
formulas: Parallel opposite sides define a parallelogram; parallel lines preserve corresponding angles.
steps: EBFD is a parallelogram, so BF=DE=AE and FD=EB.

problems.title: An equilateral triangle inside a square
problems.question: E is inside square ABCD and BCE is equilateral. Find angle AED.
problems.idea: Use the two isosceles triangles at the side vertices.
formulas: Square angles are 90°; equilateral angles are 60°; triangle angles sum to 180°.
steps: The angles around E are AEB=75°, BEC=60°, CED=75° and DEA.

problems.title: One angle equals the sum of the others
problems.question: A triangle satisfies A-B=C. What type of triangle must it be?
problems.idea: Rewrite the relation as A=B+C.
steps: Substitute B+C=A into the angle sum.

problems.title: A sum of squares can only be zero in one way
problems.question: Find x+y if $x^2-2xy+2y^2+4y+4=0$ for real x,y.
problems.idea: Complete two squares.
steps: Both squares are nonnegative. Their sum is zero only if each is zero.

problems.title: Recognize a cube of a difference
problems.question: Calculate $18^3-13^3-3\cdot18\cdot13(18-13)$.
problems.idea: Use the cube identity instead of calculating large cubes.
